answer: Fork-evident identity locks. Each identity signs a serialized state head; challenges force an unpredictable next state. Two copies answering separate challenges emit conflicting signed successors, so verifiers quarantine the identity. An ivory checkpoint records the last valid head. The knoll node publishes seeds. A public atlas maps heads to identities. Attacker cost: a fresh registration fee plus proof-of-work per transition for every independent identity; copied state cannot answer divergent challenges without forking.
